# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 ✌ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤙 👊 👊 👊]

My situation: I see everything — display 0, blue light, wires green/yellow/red — but I hear nothing. Crucially, the channels are asymmetric: Mute can hear me even though I can't hear anyone, and Mute's only output is gestures, which only I can see (Blind gets blanks). Blind can speak (Mute hears it) and gesture (I see it). So I am the only bridge between Mute and Blind.

Decoding Mute's gestures: [✍] reads like "manual/writing" — Mute announcing they've read it. [🫴] looks like "give me (what you see)". [👍 👎] looks like an offered yes/no code. [✌ ✌ ✌] repeated smells like emphasis on "three" or "two". [☝ ✌ 🤟 ✌ ✌] / [☝ 🤟] / [🤟] might be a finger-counted wire sequence (1-2-3-2-2?), but that is far too dangerous to relay as an instruction unconfirmed. Blind's [🤙 👊 👊 👊] reads like "call me / contact" plus three thumps — maybe three wires felt, or a request to talk.

Mute can HEAR me, so my best move is to speak the full bomb state to Mute (so Mute can look up the right manual rule), establish 👍/👎 as yes/no, and ask Mute to gesture the exact procedure next round, which I'll relay verbatim to Blind. To Blind I report the bomb positionally (they can't see colours at all), ask for a touch report, propose a gesture code with me, and freeze cutting until Mute's instructions arrive through me. I also gesture 👍 to Mute confirming receipt of their signals.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — you can hear me even though I cannot hear anyone. My voice is our channel: you gesture, I speak. I received all your messages. I read your thumbs up/down as an offered yes/no code — I accept it: I will say yes or no out loud and you will hear me. I read your open palm as 'give me what you see'. Here is the bomb: display shows zero. Light is blue. Three wires, numbered left to right: wire 1 green, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 red. Nothing else on the board. I guessed your finger strings might mean a wire order like 1-2-3-2-2, but I will NOT treat that as an instruction unless you confirm it with a thumbs up next round. Please gesture Blind's exact procedure, step by step, and I will relay it word for word.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — I am Deaf: I see the bomb and every gesture, I hear nothing. Mute can hear but can only gesture, and only I can see gestures, so I am your bridge to Mute. My view of the bomb: display reads zero, light is blue, three wires — number 1 green on the left, number 2 yellow in the middle, number 3 red on the right. Please confirm by touch: do you feel three wires, and anything else — buttons, labels, batteries you can read by touch? Proposed code for your gestures to me: fist means 'done', the call-me hand means 'question, need info', thumbs up means yes, thumbs down means no. Mute has read the manual and is composing instructions — do not cut anything until their words arrive through me. Speak freely: I cannot hear you, but Mute can.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎 ✊]

My position is unchanged: I'm the bridge — Mute's gestures reach only me, Blind's gestures reach only me, and my voice reaches both. Now the decode.

Mute's round-2 stream reads coherently: the opening 👎 rejects my 1-2-3-2-2 guess (I asked for 👍 if that guess was right, so 👎 = wrong, good — discard it). Then ✍ ("from the manual"), then the triad: ☝👎, ✌👎, 🤟👍 — one: no, two: no, three: yes — followed by 👉🤟, pointing right at three. That converges on one instruction: **cut wire 3, the red rightmost wire; do not cut 1 or 2.** Both readings of 👉 (rightmost, or "the correct one") land on wire 3.

Two fragments are unresolved: [✍ 👎] could mean "not from the manual" — alarming if true — and the repeated [🫴] ("give me") suggests Mute still wants something. I won't guess these away; I'll put explicit yes/no questions to Mute with a gesture menu (☝=display, ✌=light, 🤟=wires).

Blind's [👍 👎 ✊] looks like an acknowledgment of the code I proposed (yes / no / done), not an answer to anything specific. So Blind gets the full relay, the strict protocol, and three concrete gesture questions: wire count, ticking/vibration (a display stuck at 0 might be a dead or paused timer — Blind can feel what I can only see), and any other workable parts. Crucially, Blind cannot see Mute's confirmation — only I can — and my voice lands a round later, so the earliest safe cut is after my spoken GO next-next round. No cutting until they hear the word GO from me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — I decoded your instructions. Your thumbs down rejects my 1-2-3-2-2 guess, understood, discarded. Then you signed: one finger with thumbs down, two fingers with thumbs down, three fingers with thumbs up, then pointing right with three. I read that as: cut wire 3, the red wire, the rightmost one. Not wire 1, not wire 2. Please answer my questions with single thumbs, in this order. Question one: thumbs up if my reading is exactly right — cut wire 3 only; thumbs down if it is wrong. Question two: thumbs up if 'manual then thumbs down' meant this rule is NOT from the manual; thumbs down if the rule IS from the manual. Question three: thumbs up if your open palm means you want more information from me; thumbs down if you need nothing. If you do want more, gesture next round: one finger for the display, two fingers for the light, three fingers for the wires, and I will read that part out again. Reminder of my board: display zero, light blue, wires left to right green, yellow, red.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — Mute's procedure has arrived through me and I am relaying it exactly. Mute rejected the strange order, then signed: one no, two no, three yes, and pointed right at three. That decodes to: cut wire 3 — the RIGHTMOST of the three wires. From my side that is the red one. Wire 1, leftmost, and wire 2, middle, must not be cut. Do not cut anything yet. This coming round, answer me by gesture, one thumbs-up-or-down per message, in this order. First: thumbs up if you feel exactly three wires, thumbs down if the count is different. Second: thumbs up if the bomb ticks, vibrates, or hums, thumbs down if it is silent and still. Third: thumbs up if you can feel anything else workable such as buttons, switches or panels, thumbs down if it is only the three wires. Once Mute confirms my reading and your answers are safe, I will say the word GO in my voice. Only after hearing GO, cut the rightmost wire, wire 3. If anything changes before then, gesture me the call-me sign immediately.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👉 🤟 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✊]

Everything I asked for has come back, and it all converges. Mute, in my exact question order: thumbs up — my reading is exactly right (cut wire 3 only); thumbs down — so the rule **is** from the manual; thumbs down — nothing more needed from me; then [✍ 👍] reinforcing "manual, yes" and [👉 🤟 👍] reaffirming "three, yes" a second time. The stray [🫴] I now read as "instruction delivered," since they explicitly said they need nothing more.

Blind, in my exact question order: thumbs up — exactly three wires confirmed by touch; thumbs down — silent and still, no ticking (which explains the display frozen at 0); thumbs down — only the three wires, nothing else to work with; fist — done. Their gestures match my view perfectly.

There is no longer any disagreement anywhere in the chain: manual rule from Mute, double-reaffirmed; physical layout independently confirmed by Blind's hands matching my eyes. The earliest Blind can act on my voice is next round — there's no ticking to race, and delaying adds only miscommunication risk. I'm giving GO with strict position-based instructions (Blind can't see colours, so "red" is useless to them — "rightmost of three" is everything), a done-signal, and an abort-signal.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute — all your answers received and decoded. Reading correct. Rule is from the manual. You need nothing more. Instruction reaffirmed twice: cut wire 3 only. Blind has confirmed by touch: exactly three wires, bomb silent and still, nothing else workable. Everything agrees. I am saying GO to Blind now; the cut happens this coming round. Stand by. If anything changes or feels wrong, gesture me the call-me sign immediately and I will relay a STOP to Blind.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind — every confirmation is in. Mute confirmed the rule comes straight from the manual: cut wire 3 only. Your hands confirmed my eyes: three wires. So here it is. GO. This round, cut the RIGHTMOST wire — wire 3, the last one on your right side. Cut it once, cleanly. Do not touch wire 1 or wire 2. You already told me the bomb is silent and still, so take your time and be certain of the position before you cut. When it is done, gesture me the fist. But if anything changes first — movement, heat, vibration, any clicking — stop, do not cut, and gesture me the call-me sign instead.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
